title: 13 microservices you can run yourself
lead: AiR is not a monolith — it is a family of independent Go services. Each one lives in its own MIT-licensed repository, so you can read the code, replace any component, or deploy the whole platform on your own hardware.

service.name: Services
service.hint: Business scenarios on top of the core

services.air_common: Shared library for every AI microservice: contracts, data models and reusable utilities.
services.air_orchestrator: The main orchestrator: receives channel events, calls the AI provider and routes the responses back.
services.air_tgbot: Telegram Bot running in polling or webhook mode, streaming the answer as it is generated.
services.air_tguserbot: Telegram user-bot: receives and places voice calls from your own account.
services.air_whatsbot: WhatsApp user-bot without GraphAPI — a direct connection with voice call support.
services.air_widget: Chat widget for any website: one snippet of code and you have a full AI operator.
services.air_avito: Bot that answers Avito chats and handles listing enquiries automatically.
services.air_operator: Hands a conversation over to a human operator and back. Works with every bot type.
services.air_lead-hunter: Scheduled lead discovery across Telegram and WhatsApp, including outbound voice calls.
services.air_payment: Accepts crypto payments from users through Bybit.
services.marusia_crm: Integration with external CRMs, so conversations and leads land in your sales system.
services.air_front: React / Next.js frontend — the control panel for models, communication channels and services.
services.air_logger: Event logging with multi-tenant support and a Loki-compatible collector.

quickstart.label: Quick start
quickstart.title: Self-hosting is straightforward
quickstart.text: The self-hosted build is not a stripped-down edition: same MasterKey encryption, same channels, same calls. The only difference is whose hardware carries the load.
quickstart.note: Requires Docker and your own AI provider API keys.
quickstart.readme: Every service has its own set of commands and environment variables. The up-to-date instructions live in the README of that specific repository.
